Done. Built, tested, run, journaled, committed (f864821, 08968fd, 6ec6715).

## What got built

`tests/double_decoder.py` — your idea as tiny math model. Task: 3-digit addition `abc+def=`. Dataset engineered exactly as you said — each prompt two responses:
- **quick thinking** (7 chars): right-to-left column digits + carries (the hard part)
- **polished answer** (4 digits)

Three models, d=64:
- **Thinker**: 2-layer bidirectional decoder, discrete diffusion (masked-denoise training, 6-step confidence-scheduled unmasking at inference)
- **Talker**: 2-layer causal AR on `[prompt;SEP;think;SEP;answer]`
- **Baseline**: 4-layer single AR, depth/param-matched (~137k vs ~140k params)

Plus your variant 2: thinker samples 8 candidate thoughts, talker picks winner by its own answer log-prob.

## Results (500 held-out problems, exact match)

| train steps | baseline AR | double-decoder | best-of-8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 150 | 0.8% / 5.4% | **13.4% / 32.0%** | 8.8% / 18.8% |
| 300 | 20.4% / 91.6% | **89.6% / 98.8%** | 75.0% / 81.4% |
| 600 | 99.8% / 100% | 93.4% / 99.0% | 86.8% / 94.8% |
| 1200 | **100%** | 98.8% | 93.8% |

(two seeds per row; full run = 57 s wall, CPU — GPU was 100% full, nothing killed)

## Findings

1. **Your "reduce load" hypothesis confirmed** — in the low-budget regime the split learns ~4-10x faster. Decomposition moves carry logic into the parallel denoiser; talker's job becomes near-copying.
2. **Talker given ground-truth thoughts = 100% accuracy at every budget.** All residual error is the thinker. So scale the thinker, shrink the talker.
3. **Variant 2 (explore many, talker picks best) fails as specced** — best-of-8 lost to single greedy thought at every budget. Talker is confidently fluent on wrong scratchpads; its log-prob is no verifier. Needs trained verifier head or consistency voting instead.
4. **Crossover at ~600 steps**: with enough compute, single AR saturates on this easy task. Advantage is sample/compute efficiency, not capacity. Harder tasks (5+ digits, multiplication) would test whether baseline ever catches up.

## Process

Sandbox-first per AGENTS.md: 12 proving tests + 1 e2e, all written before/with the module, 13/13 pass. One real bug caught: untrained sampler could draw MASK_ID and never unmask — fixed by banning special tokens + final argmax fill. `make lint` exit 0, `make pyaot` 83 files 0 errors, docs/functions.md entries for all 16 functions, full journal entries. Suite verified piecewise due to GPU contention: 219 pass on CPU, 16/16 CUDA flex tests pass on GPU; `tests/e2e/test_train_entry.py` unrun (GPU full, CPU too slow) — journaled as owed, my change touches only tests/ so no pipeline risk.
